title: What an anchored comparison must balance on a non-collapsible scale
question: On the log odds ratio scale a purely prognostic covariate changes the marginal effect. Does an anchored MAIC that balances only covariate means, as practice does, leave material bias, and does balancing the variance of the prognostic index remove it at acceptable cost in effective sample size?
design: Anchored and unanchored binary-outcome comparisons, 108 cells crossing prognostic strength, the source-to-target ratio of prognostic index variance, target mean shift and effect modification; five methods including MAIC on means, on means and variances, on the prognostic index variance, and G-computation. 1000 replicates per cell.
answer: Yes. On the log odds ratio scale a difference in the spread of prognosis between trials biases an anchored MAIC that balances only means by up to 0.11, even with no effect modification. Balancing variances or the variance of the prognostic index removes the bias, but when the source is less dispersed than the target the loss of effective sample size makes RMSE worse than not balancing. G-computation was unbiased with the lowest RMSE throughout.
findings: MAIC on means biased by 0.05 to 0.11 in the 12 primary anchored scenarios, beyond 0.05 (95% Monte Carlo interval) in 9; registered verdict CONFIRMED.
Unadjusted anchored bias on the exact population bias: slope 0.981 (SE 0.018).
Balancing variances cut the bias to at most 0.08 (0.02 in all but one scenario) but dropped effective sample size to 44 to 284 of 1000 when the source index variance was half the target's.
G-computation: largest absolute bias 0.024 anchored and 0.020 unanchored, lowest RMSE in every primary scenario.
not_answered: Independent normal covariates and a correctly specified outcome model favor G-computation. Hazard ratios, skewed covariates and augmented estimators not run; MAIC intervals treat weights as fixed. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target population
methods_compared: MAIC on means and the prognostic index variance
